queries.title: SELECT … ORDER BY … LIMIT
queries.sql: SELECT id, name, country FROM customers ORDER BY id LIMIT $1
queries.note: Pick columns, sort, and keep the first N rows. Without ORDER BY the row order is not guaranteed, so LIMIT would return arbitrary rows.

queries.title: WHERE with a bound parameter
queries.sql: SELECT id, name, country FROM customers WHERE country = $1 ORDER BY name
queries.note: The country travels as a parameter ($1), never pasted into the SQL text. That is what stops SQL injection.

queries.title: Ranges: >= and < (half-open)
queries.sql:
SELECT name, price FROM products
WHERE price >= 20 AND price < 60
ORDER BY price DESC
queries.note: Half-open ranges (>= start AND < end) never double-count a boundary value, unlike BETWEEN, which includes both ends.

queries.title: IN (list)
queries.sql: SELECT name, category FROM products WHERE category IN ('Books', 'Games') ORDER BY category, name
queries.note: IN is shorthand for several OR'ed equality tests. `= ANY(%s)` does the same with an array parameter.

queries.title: Pattern matching: LIKE / ILIKE
queries.sql: SELECT name, description FROM products WHERE description ILIKE '%usb%' ORDER BY name
queries.note: ILIKE is case-insensitive LIKE. % matches any run of characters, _ exactly one. A leading % cannot use a B-tree index (see the trigram demo).

queries.title: WRONG: = NULL
queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM customers WHERE referred_by = NULL
queries.note: NULL means 'unknown', and unknown = unknown is not true, so this matches nothing. Always.

queries.title: RIGHT: IS NULL
queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM customers WHERE referred_by IS NULL
queries.note: IS NULL / IS NOT NULL (or IS DISTINCT FROM) are the only reliable NULL tests.

queries.title: DISTINCT
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers ORDER BY country
queries.note: Removes duplicate rows from the result.

queries.title: DISTINCT ON (Postgres extension)
queries.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (category) category, name, price
FROM products
ORDER BY category, price DESC
queries.note: Keeps the first row of each group, as decided by ORDER BY: here the most expensive product per category. A Postgres-only shortcut for 'top 1 per group'.

queries.title: Expressions, CASE, COALESCE, aliases
queries.sql:
SELECT name, price,
       round(price * 1.2, 2) AS price_with_vat,
       CASE WHEN price < 30 THEN 'budget'
            WHEN price < 100 THEN 'mid'
            ELSE 'premium' END AS band,
       coalesce(attrs->>'color', 'n/a') AS color
FROM products ORDER BY price LIMIT 8
queries.note: Compute new columns on the fly. CASE is SQL's if/else; COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument.

queries.title: FETCH FIRST … WITH TIES
queries.sql:

FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS WITH TIES
queries.note: Standard-SQL LIMIT. WITH TIES also returns rows that tie with the last one, so equally priced products are not cut arbitrarily.

queries.title: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
queries.sql: INSERT INTO stock VALUES ('apple', 99) ON CONFLICT (sku) DO NOTHING RETURNING sku
queries.note: Insert if new, silently skip if the key exists. RETURNING shows nothing for skipped rows.

queries.title: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (upsert)
queries.sql:
INSERT INTO stock VALUES ('apple', 3), ('plum', 7)
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE SET qty = stock.qty + EXCLUDED.qty
RETURNING sku, qty, (xmax = 0) AS inserted
queries.note: EXCLUDED is the row that failed to insert. apple existed, so its qty was increased; plum is new. xmax = 0 is a known trick to tell inserts from updates.

queries.title: MERGE … RETURNING merge_action()
queries.sql:
MERGE INTO stock s
USING delivery d ON s.sku = d.sku
WHEN MATCHED AND d.qty = 0 THEN DELETE
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET qty = s.qty + d.qty
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT VALUES (d.sku, d.qty)
RETURNING merge_action() AS action, s.sku, s.qty
queries.note: MERGE (SQL standard) applies a delivery file in one statement: delete, update or insert per row. RETURNING merge_action() arrived in Postgres 17.

queries.title: GROUP BY with count / sum / avg / min / max
queries.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       count(*)                  AS lines,
       sum(oi.qty)               AS units,
       sum(oi.qty * oi.unit_price) AS revenue,
       round(avg(oi.unit_price), 2) AS avg_price,
       min(oi.unit_price) AS min_price, max(oi.unit_price) AS max_price
FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC
queries.note: One output row per category. Every selected column is either in GROUP BY or inside an aggregate.

queries.title: HAVING filters groups
queries.sql:
SELECT c.name, sum(oi.qty * oi.unit_price) AS revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING sum(oi.qty * oi.unit_price) >= $1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
queries.note: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the groups after. Here: customers who spent at least the threshold.

queries.title: FILTER and count(DISTINCT)

SELECT count(*) AS orders,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid')      AS paid,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'shipped')   AS shipped,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'cancelled') AS cancelled,
       count(DISTINCT customer_id) AS distinct_customers
FROM orders
queries.note: FILTER (WHERE …) turns one pass over the table into several conditional counts (a pivot).

queries.title: ROLLUP (subtotals and grand total)

SELECT p.category, o.status, sum(oi.qty) AS units
FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE p.category IN ('Books', 'Games')
GROUP BY ROLLUP (p.category, o.status)
ORDER BY p.category NULLS LAST, o.status NULLS LAST
queries.note: ROLLUP adds subtotal rows (status = NULL) and a grand total (both NULL). GROUPING SETS and CUBE give other combinations.

queries.title: row_number / rank / dense_rank
queries.sql:
SELECT category, name, price,
       row_number() OVER w AS row_number,
       rank()       OVER w AS rank,
       dense_rank() OVER w AS dense_rank
FROM products
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC)
ORDER BY category, price DESC
queries.note: A window function computes over related rows without collapsing them. PARTITION BY restarts the numbering per category.

queries.title: Running total, lag, moving average, % of total
queries.sql:
SELECT month, revenue,
       sum(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS running_total,
       revenue - lag(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS vs_prev_month,
       round(avg(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS moving_avg_3m,
       round(100 * revenue / sum(revenue) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_total
FROM (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)::date AS month, sum(oi.qty * oi.unit_price) AS revenue
  FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY 1
) m ORDER BY month
queries.note: ORDER BY inside OVER makes a running window; ROWS BETWEEN sets the frame; an empty OVER () spans every row.

queries.title: timestamptz, AT TIME ZONE and interval across a DST change
queries.sql:
SELECT timestamptz '2026-03-28 12:00 Europe/Berlin' AS start_berlin,
       timestamptz '2026-03-28 12:00 Europe/Berlin' AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS start_utc_wall_clock,
       timestamptz '2026-03-28 12:00 Europe/Berlin' + interval '1 day' AS plus_1_day,

queries.title: -> and ->> operators
queries.sql:
SELECT name, attrs,
       attrs -> 'color'  AS color_json,
       attrs ->> 'color' AS color_text,
       (attrs ->> 'wireless')::boolean AS wireless
FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' ORDER BY name
queries.note: -> returns jsonb (keeps quotes and type), ->> returns text. Cast ->> to compare numbers or booleans.

queries.title: @> containment (uses a GIN index)
queries.sql: SELECT name, attrs FROM products WHERE attrs @> $1::jsonb ORDER BY name
queries.note: Does the document contain this sub-document? The most index-friendly JSONB operator.

queries.title: ? key exists
queries.sql: SELECT name, attrs FROM products WHERE attrs ? 'wireless' ORDER BY name
queries.note: Rows whose document has the top-level key, whatever its value.

queries.title: SQL/JSON path: @@ and jsonb_path_query
queries.sql:
SELECT name, jsonb_path_query_first(attrs, '$.pages') AS pages
FROM products WHERE attrs @@ '$.pages > 400' ORDER BY name
queries.note: JSON path expressions filter and extract inside documents, like XPath for JSON.

queries.title: Modify: ||, jsonb_set, - (removes a key)
queries.sql:
SELECT name,
       attrs || '{"on_sale": true}'                 AS merged,
       jsonb_set(attrs, '{color}', '"purple"')      AS recolored,
       attrs - 'color'                              AS without_color
FROM products WHERE id = 5
queries.note: These return new values; wrap them in UPDATE … SET attrs = … to save.

queries.title: Build JSON: jsonb_build_object, jsonb_agg
queries.sql:
SELECT category, jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('name', name, 'price', price) ORDER BY price) AS items
FROM products WHERE category IN ('Games', 'Garden') GROUP BY category
queries.note: Shape API responses straight in SQL.
